title: Ruins of Hoanna
summary: Destroyed towns, old catacombs and modern shafts

blocks.text: Goal: find a ruin. After MRU wrecked Hoanna, three kinds of ruins were left behind: destroyed towns on the surface, old catacombs buried underground and modern shafts below sea level. The titanite and void materials in their chests feed the next few chapters; see [[hoanna/relics]].

Only on land, roughly one every <t>512</t> blocks, about a hundred blocks across. A few <t>concrete</t> roads run out from the centre, following the lie of the land, lined with houses, towers and decorations.

items: Towers: four stacked frames of {item:essentialcraft5:fortified_stone}, narrowing towards the top, about 64 blocks tall. The ring of fortified stone near the top, about 57 blocks above the ground, holds 4 chests. A town usually has two to five towers.

Houses: fortified stone walls with {item:essentialcraft5:fortified_glass} windows, two to ten storeys, rooms full of {item:essentialcraft5:concrete} rubble. Everything above the ground floor has partly collapsed, worse the higher you go; the ground floor is mostly intact. A {item:essentialcraft5:levitator} is buried under each corner.
Spreader posts: four {item:essentialcraft5:fortified_stone_fence} posts around a {item:essentialcraft5:magic_fence} post, topped with a {item:essentialcraft5:spreader}.
Lamp posts: a {item:essentialcraft5:void_fence} post capped with {item:essentialcraft5:void_stone}, with invisible lights beside it, so the area stays lit at night.
Craters: blast holes in the ground and inside buildings, the biggest almost twenty blocks across.

blocks.caption: No recipes: these three blocks only come from ruins

blocks.text: Old Catacombs lie deep in the stone (around <t>y 6–32</t>): small 5-block rooms of {item:essentialcraft5:fortified_stone} joined by corridors thirty to sixty-odd blocks long, sprawling more than a hundred blocks out from the central room. They can sit under any kind of Hoanna terrain, roughly one every two hundred blocks.

The way in: a square chimney poking out of the ground, rimmed with {item:essentialcraft5:fortified_stone} and lined with a full column of ladders, is a catacomb exit. Climb all the way down to reach the exit room, where a chest sits on a block of {item:essentialcraft5:void_stone} in the middle of the floor. See [[hoanna/relics]] for what it holds.

items: About one room in ten is an exit room, and every exit room has a chest. About one catacomb in five has no exit room at all — no chimney and no chest.
Some rooms have half caved in, leaving heaps of {item:essentialcraft5:concrete} rubble; others are overgrown with leaves that never wither, with {item:essentialcraft5:root} pushing through the floor.
The walls are {item:essentialcraft5:fortified_stone}, slower to mine than stone. The corridors are long and straight, so bring plenty of torches and keep your bearings.

blocks.text: Modern Shafts lie below sea level. They look like vanilla abandoned mineshafts, except the supports every few blocks are made of different stuff: {item:essentialcraft5:void_fence} posts, with {item:essentialcraft5:void_stone} beams and void stone patching the gaps in the floor. If you want to mine void stone directly, this is the place — a single shaft holds well over a thousand blocks. There is roughly one every two hundred and fifty blocks.

items: Some corridors have rails, and now and then a {item:minecraft:chest_minecart} carrying the usual abandoned mineshaft loot.
A corridor full of cobwebs hides a cave spider spawner. Cave spiders poison you, so have a plan for breaking the spawner before you get close.

blocks.title: Don't linger
blocks.text: Searching a whole ruin means a long stay in Hoanna, and radiation keeps building up; see [[hoanna/radiation]].

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: You walk into any destroyed town, old catacomb or modern shaft; this step ticks itself off.

The original research book calls Hoanna a terrible place: empty ruined cities under a scorching sun and catacombs below, the remains of a past civilisation, which now and then still hide a chest or two. The English book calls the first two destroyed cities and underground catacombs.
